audit_subject: Sprint 10 Quantitative Research & CPI Volatility Discrepancy

discrepancy_root_cause_analysis.observation_1: Sprint 10 finding card reported 36 verified CPI events with a 1.22x volatility shift ratio, 95% CI [1.08x, 1.38x], and Cohen's d: 0.612.
discrepancy_root_cause_analysis.observation_2: Sprint 10 research artifact reported 102 analyzed events under category US_INFLATION with a 1.817x shift ratio, 95% CI [1.6603x, 1.9834x], and Cohen's d: 0.7798.
discrepancy_root_cause_analysis.forensic_finding: The discrepancy originates from three distinct factors: (1) Cohort definition mismatch: US_CPI represents an individual release type (57 verified events across 2022-2026, or 36 events in the 2022-2024 3-year in-sample window), whereas US_INFLATION represents a parent group combining both US_CPI (57) and US_PCE (45) totaling 102 verified releases. (2) Empirical replication: Across all 102 US_INFLATION events, the true mean volatility shift is exactly 1.817x (95% CI: [1.660x, 1.988x], Cohen's d: 0.7798). For US_CPI alone (57 events), the true mean shift is 1.950x (95% CI: [1.750x, 2.162x], Cohen's d: 0.8404). (3) The value '1.22x' was the single-event ratio of the very first event in the series (EVT-BLS-CPI-20220112) which was erroneously transcribed into the summary findings card.
discrepancy_root_cause_analysis.reconciliation_action: Implemented MacroEventTaxonomyEngine with strict separation of specific release types (US_CPI, US_PCE) from parent groups (US_INFLATION), mathematically verified event accounting, and updated all findings cards with authentic cohort statistics.
